candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — infection-prevention principles and historical Universal Precautions
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the historical purpose of Universal Precautions: blood/body-fluid precautions applied regardless of a patient's known bloodborne infection status during the HIV/AIDS era.

options.A: Universal Precautions developed during the HIV/AIDS era and applied blood and specified body-fluid precautions to all patients regardless of known infection status.
options.B: Universal Precautions began as a food-safety program and were later transferred to hospitals to address occupational blood exposure.
options.C: Universal Precautions required isolation of every hospitalized patient regardless of diagnosis, symptoms, or anticipated blood exposure.
options.D: Universal Precautions replaced hand hygiene and personal protective equipment with environmental disinfection as the principal control.

candidate.rationale: CDC's historical isolation-guideline table identifies Universal Precautions in 1985–1988 as having developed in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic and applying Blood and Body Fluid precautions to all patients regardless of infection status. It also included PPE, handwashing, and sharps recommendations. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Universal Precautions were developed in response to HIV/AIDS and applied specified blood/body-fluid precautions regardless of known infection status.
